decision: Use one canonical lease/QA campaign plus three lightweight run-scoped committed-response recovery campaigns, driven by a sequential qualification runner.

correctness.winner: run-scoped fault-only crash-after-commit service plus independent campaign IDs
correctness.reason: Exercises durable reconciliation with fresh request/idempotency identities and preserves durable state between runs instead of deleting it.

security_transport.reason: Normal qrexec service remains unchanged; crash behavior is only reachable through the separately policy-scoped synthetic fault service.

performance_regression.winner: one 31-second lease/QA run plus three lightweight recovery runs
performance_regression.reason: Produces at least three recovery samples without paying the lease-expiry wait three times; no new daemon, database, or worker round trip outside qualification.

alternatives.name: repeat the full lease/QA campaign three times
alternatives.failure_lesson: Correct but wastes roughly two extra lease-expiry waits and adds no proportional coverage value.

alternatives.name: keep DIG_CRASH_AFTER_REQUEST_ID fixed
alternatives.failure_lesson: Conflicts with run-scoped request IDs and can silently reuse durable journal evidence across qualification runs.

alternatives.name: clear mission/journal state between runs
alternatives.failure_lesson: Destroys the persistence/reconciliation conditions the qualification is intended to prove.

qa_expectations: unique run IDs and run-scoped request/idempotency identities
at least three recovery latency samples
lease fencing and QA before/after join exercised
no duplicate committed mutations, unresolved pending requests, stale completions, or QA-before-join
same git SHA, source Qube, target Qube, service, and qrexec transport across the qualification set
safety: Synthetic defensive qualification only. No real financial transactions, payment data, or weakening of security controls.
